key_insight: LeanPRM uses Lean to automatically generate step-level labels for natural-language proofs, enabling scalable process supervision without human annotation.
engineering_relevance: It provides a practical training pipeline for stronger proof verifiers and better best-of-N proof selection in theorem proving systems.
method: A model writes a natural-language proof paired with a formal Lean proof.
Lean checks each step and assigns labels from the formal verification outcome.
A second model filters syntax-only Lean failures so negatives reflect mathematical mistakes.
evidence_signal: On LeanPRM-Bench, a Qwen3-4B verifier improved exact step-label accuracy from 48.2% to 74.7%, outperforming the same model trained on PRM800K.
watch_item: Performance depends on generating aligned formal proofs, and any mismatch between Lean syntax errors and true mathematical errors must be carefully filtered.
paper_title: LeanPRM: Lean-Grounded Process Supervision for Natural Language Proof Verification
